description: §19.10.3 (S453/B1a, RULED) — leaving a `transaction { }` by `return` ROLLs IT BACK; only normal completion COMMITs (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"). transfer(4, false) debits account 1 and credits account 2 and the block completes, so it COMMITs (6 / 4). transfer(100, true) debits account 1 to -94 and then `return`s out of the block from inside an `if` — the block ROLLs BACK, so account 1 is still 6 and account 2 still 4. Pre-S453 that second shape was a compile error (the S450 interim E-TRANSACTION-CONTROL-FLOW refusal), so it was not expressible in scrml source at all; this case is what the ruling buys, and a codes-only case cannot see it — the proof is the two balances read back after the bail.
rationale: §19.10.3 (S453): "A `return`, or a `break` / `continue` whose target is outside the block, SHALL roll the transaction back before the exit proceeds; only normal completion COMMITs." §19.10.4: "No transaction SHALL be left open." Provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S449 (B1a) — "`return` / `break` / `continue` out of a `transaction {}` block ROLLS BACK — only normal completion commits".
